newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BRAZIL SEES $3-4 BLN OIL INVESTMENT IN NEXT 3 YRS.
newsitem.headline: BRAZIL SEES $3-4 BLN OIL INVESTMENT IN NEXT 3 YRS.

text.p: Brazil will receive at least $3 billion to $4 billion in oil investment in the next three years as a result of the end of the state's monopoly of the sector, Mines and Energy Minister Raimundo Brito said on Thursday.

"The minimum goal is that in the first three years, we will have attracted investments in exploration and development totalling $3 billion to $4 billion," Brito said in an interview on local television.
Brito said the funds will come from some 60 new partnerships now being negotiated between state-owned Petrobras and local and foreign private firms.
President Fernando Henrique Cardoso signed into law Wednesday a bill that regulates the end of the Brazilian state's oil monopoly and opens the sector to competition.
"We can have contracts where Petrobras can be a majority or minority partner," he told O Globo television. "These negotiations are advanced."
Brito did not name the firms negotiating with giant Petrobras but said they included major world oil companies.
Petrobras, Brazil's largest state company, and the Brazilians would benefit from the end of the state's monopoly of the sector.
"We'll have a stronger, more competitive Petrobras and, with that, the Brazilian people...win," he said.
